author: Inside Edition
description: Country singer Michael Ray got trapped inside the bathroom on his flight from Nashville to San Francisco. The Southwest Airlines crew tried to free him but the door would not budge. Ray reassured his rescuers through the crack in the door. Eventually, maintenance was called to help. Inside Edition spoke with Ray after he landed at New York's LaGuardia Airport on his way to perform in the Big Apple.
title: Country Singer Michael Ray Stuck In Airplane Bathroom

author: Inside Edition
description: There was dramatic testimony in the Ohio trial of a former "American Idol" contestant who's accused of killing his wife, Ashley Flynn. Caleb Flynn broke down in tears on the first day of his trial as the court heard about a text message he sent to his mistress saying, "I could literally kill her." Flynn had pleaded not guilty and the trial is expected to last two weeks. If convicted, Flynn could be sentenced to life in prison without parole. Inside Edition's Steven Fabian reports.
title: Former 'American Idol' Contestant Breaks Down In Tears At His Murder Trial

author: Inside Edition
description: It's an odd story about how a stray cat brought attention to a new species of animal. National Geographic says one of their explorers working in Bolivia in 2017 got a call from a local animal sanctuary, claiming they had a "weird cat" on their hands. The cat was reportedly surrendered to the sanctuary after a man housed it for a whole year, thinking it was just a stray domesticated cat. Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: New Species Of Cat Found In Bolivia

author: Inside Edition
description: Police say Flock surveillance cameras are helping them catch criminals across America. The high-tech cameras use license plate reading technology, enabling cops to track peoples' movements behind the wheel. But there are questions now being raised about who's watching the watchers? In the past two years, privacy groups say over two dozen rogue cops have been accused of misusing Flock's cameras to allegedly stalk their romantic partners. Now, Flock's founders are announcing new mandatory safeguards aimed at preventing cops from misusing their cameras.
title: Who's Watching the Watchers? Inside the Flock Surveillance Camera Controversy
